# Meet Amazon Quick: The AI Wizard Revolving your Desktop

Amazon Quick is an AWS AI assistant for desktop and web, which connects to work data and applications. The video shows the native app for macOS and Windows, the dashboards created by natural language, integration with Excel and Gmail and the productivity gain that the tool promises.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on May 7, 2026 (8 min 55 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=thzcsZ2yjtA

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## The cost of manual labor

Who manages teams loses the day with manual tasks: switch between messages, emails, spreadsheets and presentations, and copy information from one side to the other [00:42]. Disconnected flows force people to serve as a bridge between systems that do not talk [01:46].

Hand-formatted reports and time-consuming BI panels leave isolated data: information exists but does not arrive in time to base a decision [02:08].

## What is Amazon Quick

Quick is an AI wizard for desktop and web that connects data and applications to turn questions into actions [02:29]. According to the video, it is proactive: it sets up a graph of personal knowledge and learns the priorities, projects and relations of the organization [02:29].

Quick is now a native app for macOS and Windows [02:50]. It reads local files without uploading, sends system notifications, such as a conflict warning in the agenda, and shares the memory between the web and the desktop [03:10].

## Dashboards by natural language

Setting up an analytical panel took hours or days of manual configuration [03:30]. With Amazon QuickSight's Generate Analysis feature, integrated with Quick, the effort drops to minutes [03:52]. The process has three steps:

- Describe the objective of the analysis [04:13].
- Choose up to three data sets [04:13].
- Review the generated dashboard. The system chooses the graphs, creates the filters and adds calculated fields, such as growth year by year [04:34].

An example of request: "Create a sales performance dashboard with revenue trends and monthly growth" [04:34]. The panel is editable, and the team can refine and publish the result [04:55].

## Excel, Gmail and other integrations

Quick analyzes a local Excel spreadsheet and creates dynamic tables [05:15]. In the same window, it extracts the main points from the table, writes an email draft in Gmail and can generate a PowerPoint presentation [05:36].

It also integrates with Google Calendar, Zoom, Airtable, Slack, QuickBooks and Salesforce [05:58].

## Productivity Gain

For the video, the biggest gain is to have one place for tools and data, which reduces the context exchange between platforms [06:39].

Migrating Power BI or Tableau panels to QuickSight would take months. According to the video, with AWS agents Transform takes days [07:00].

Quick Automate has a shared file storage in the app. A list of contacts or a dragged price table to the interface is available for automation flows [07:42].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Amazon Quick work outside the browser?

Yeah. It has native app for macOS and Windows, in addition to the web version [02:50].

### How many data sets can a dashboard use?

Up to three, according to the video [04:13].
